rootCause: IlGenerator.GenerateIl indexed `instructionMap[target][0]` for a branch target without checking the list was non-empty. Generation is allowed to emit nothing for an instruction - a constructor call the allocation already covers is dropped - and a jump or conditional jump over one of those had nothing to bind to. The same guard was already present two loops earlier for `blockEntryMap` (`generated.Count > 0`) and in `ResolveBlockEntryInstruction`, so only the direct-instruction path lacked it. compilerError: none - it compiled and was wrong
observed: `DateTime value = default(DateTime); return default(DateTime).CompareTo(value);` - both DateTimes zero, so CompareTo always returns 0 and every comparison of two TimeInGames reads as equal.
expected: `var thisDate = new DateTime(Year, Month, Day, Hours, Minutes, Second); ... return thisDate.CompareTo(otherDate);`
rootCause: IlGenerator drops a `.ctor` call outside a constructor, on the grounds that C# cannot call a constructor on an object that already exists and the object is constructed at the `newobj` already. That is true of a reference type and false of a value type: there is no allocation to fuse with, il2cpp calls the constructor on the address of the slot holding the value, and that is exactly what C# compiles `x = new T(...)` to. The receiver load in the same case already emits the address for a value type, so not dropping the call is all that was needed.

observed: 146 CS1061 in Assembly-CSharp naming a private field of a framework generic: 68 `List<T>._version`, 35 `_items`, 34 `_size`, 7 `bool.m_value`, 2 `_syncRoot`.
expected: nothing better is available - see the root cause
rootCause: Measured rather than assumed. The read side of the trivial-accessor pairing already covers `_size`: all 34 of its occurrences in Assembly-CSharp are *writes* (`list._size = num`), and `List<T>.Count` has no public setter, so there is nothing to pair with. `_items` is 35 reads and 0 writes, and `List<T>` has no public property returning `T[]` - the nearest is the indexer, which takes an argument the field access does not have. `_version` is an enumeration-invalidation counter with no public surface at all. So every one of these is il2cpp having inlined the body of `List<T>.Add` or an enumerator into the caller, and the assembly the export compiles against is the real `List<T>`, which has no public way to say what the recovered body does. The export is faithful and the compiler is right to reject it. Fixing it would mean expressing the inlined body as the call it was inlined from, which is a different and much larger problem than accessor pairing.
evidence: probe over AccessorDefinitionFor for List`1::_size: `Capacity body did not match, wantOffset=18` and then nothing for `Count`, which is what a successful pairing looks like

compilerError: CS0117 (5) and text that is not C#
observed: `base._002Ector(...)`, which names a member no type has
rootCause: `IlGenerator.HoistBaseConstructorCall` already moves the call to the front of the body, which is the only place C# can write one. ILSpy will not fold a base call in a method that carries a stack type mismatch, whatever position it is in, so this is behind DECOMP-0004 rather than being its own defect.
